episodes.201461: During the afternoon hours of June 3rd, 2025, storms brought widespread heavy rain, flash flooding, damaging wind gusts, and a couple tornadoes to portions of Missouri. Two tornadoes impacted Jackson County, with an EF-0 near the Truman Sports Complex and an EF-1 in Independence.
episodes.201532: An upper low moved across the desert southwest June 1st into June 2nd helping to pull up higher moisture from former Tropical Storm Alvin in the eastern Pacific. Widespread showers and storms developed across New Mexico during the day June 2nd as the upper low moved into the state. Storms resulted in severe wind gusts in Clovis, penny size hail and flash flooding in Albuquerque and Farmington. Flash flooding in the north diversion arroyo channel in east central Albuquerque resulted in a fatality. Storms across the state tapered off after sunset with the loss of daytime heating and the system exiting east of the state. A 2nd upper low approached the state on June 3rd resulting in the diurnal development of storms across the Four Corners area. Storms brought quarter size hail and flash flooding to the Farmington area. ||Another round of showers and storms developed across western NM on June 4th as the upper low entered the state. These storms moved east across the state bringing flash flooding and large hail to parts of the middle Rio Grande Valley and east central New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours before exiting into the Texas Panhandle just before midnight. More rounds of severe storms developed along the dryline across far eastern New Mexico during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 5th and 6th. These storms brought large hail 1 to 2 inches in diameter to Curry and Roosevelt Counties both days and western Union County on June 6th. Additionally, several brief tornadoes were observed across east central and southeast Roosevelt County on June 5th.||Key Impacts: Hail, Flash Flood, Tornado, Severe Thunderstorm Wind Gust.
episodes.201543: A severe thunderstorm tracked across northern Weld and Logan Counties producing large hail.
episodes.201589: Severe thunderstorms, including a tornado occurred during the afternoon of June 3rd. A line of thunderstorms then moved through during the evening. Quarter size hail and damaging wind gusts also occurred, mainly across central Missouri, north of Interstate 44.
episodes.201648: In the late afternoon of June 3rd, a line of thunderstorms developed in northeast Missouri, and spread into far southeast Iowa and Illinois.  These storms rapidly became severe. The thunderstorms quickly moved northeast across southeast Iowa, west central, and northwest Illinois between 530 PM and 8 PM CDT.  This line of storms produced 8 tornadoes, along with isolated pockets of higher end wind damage from estimated winds of 80 to 100 mph. A cluster of several tornadoes moved into the the southern portions of the Quad Cities IA/IL metro area, producing EF1 damage into Moline Illinois.
episodes.201649: In the late afternoon of June 3rd, a line of thunderstorms developed in northeast Missouri, and spread into far southeast Iowa and Illinois.  These storms rapidly became severe. The thunderstorms quickly moved northeast across southeast Iowa, west central, and northwest Illinois between 530 PM and 8 PM CDT.  This line of storms produced 8 tornadoes, along with isolated pockets of higher end wind damage from estimated winds of 80 to 100 mph. A cluster of several tornadoes moved into the the southern portions of the Quad Cities IA/IL metro area, producing EF1 damage into Moline Illinois.
episodes.201650: In the late afternoon of June 3rd, a line of thunderstorms developed in northeast Missouri, and spread into far southeast Iowa and Illinois.  These storms rapidly became severe. The thunderstorms quickly moved northeast across southeast Iowa, west central, and northwest Illinois between 530 PM and 8 PM CDT.  This line of storms produced 8 tornadoes, along with isolated pockets of higher end wind damage from estimated winds of 80 to 100 mph. A cluster of several tornadoes moved into the the southern portions of the Quad Cities IA/IL metro area, producing EF1 damage into Moline Illinois.
episodes.201939: Scattered thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the second producing severe wind gusts across the South Plains and extreme southern Texas Panhandle. A strong short wave trough moved across southern Arizona into New Mexico bringing robust large scale ascent to West Texas. Very strong surface heating with temperatures warming into the 90s created a deeply mixed boundary layer. Thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon with a quick erosion of a cap, however, the warm surface temperatures kept cloud bases very high. As a result, numerous severe outflow winds were observed from this thunderstorm activity. Several locations around the South Plains incurred damage from the intense winds.
episodes.202135: A QLCS moved into northeast and central Missouri during the late afternoon on June 3rd. This feature caused wind damage in aforementioned areas before weakening. Later that evening, flooding was reported in Ralls, Montgomery, and Callaway counties as thunderstorms continued to train over those areas.
episodes.202446: Several lines or clusters of thunderstorms with damaging winds affected southern WI during the afternoon and evening. The storms occurred along a warm front and cold front as low pressure tracked from southwest WI to northeast WI.
episodes.202630: An incoming trough, upslope flow, and a somewhat weak dryline resulted in the development of scattered thunderstorms across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. A few of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail. The two most notable storms occurred in Fort Stockton and Pleasant Farms. Microbursts in these locations resulted in winds in excess of 100 mph and widespread damage to roofs and mobile homes. Two people were injured in Pleasant Farms.
episodes.202643: During the early afternoon of June 2nd, scattered storms developed over parts of eastern New Mexico and the far southwestern Texas Panhandle. These storms quickly grew in coverage expanding northward into a line before moving easterly across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. Some of these storms were severe with the main impact being damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202671: Scattered severe thunderstorms impacted portions of western and northern Oklahoma on the afternoon and evening of the 2nd. The combination of strong instability and sufficient wind shear (aided by the passage of a weak shortwave trough) promoted organized thunderstorms. A few reports of large hail and thunderstorm wind damage were received across the aforementioned areas.
episodes.202672: Widespread severe thunderstorms, organized along a passing cold front, impacted much of Oklahoma and western-north Texas on the afternoon and evening of the 3rd. In addition to reports and observations of thunderstorm wind damage and large hail, six tornadoes occurred across the WFO Norman Forecast Area. Flash flooding also occurred during the evening hours across southeastern Oklahoma due to repeated rounds of heavy thunderstorms.
episodes.202673: Widespread severe thunderstorms, organized along a passing cold front, impacted much of Oklahoma and western-north Texas on the afternoon and evening of the 3rd. In addition to reports and observations of thunderstorm wind damage and large hail, six tornadoes occurred across the WFO Norman Forecast Area.
episodes.202718: Locally heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in quick, but brief rises on smaller creeks and streams in the immediate area. These elevated levels quickly fell back below flood stage as water moved downstream.
episodes.202754: On 6/3, slow moving front resulted in several rounds of thunderstorms across northeast Kansas. This resulted in rainfall amounts of 2 to 6 inches and a few instances of water rescues and street flooding.
episodes.203037: In the late afternoon of the 2nd, a cluster of storms formed in far western Kansas and proceeded to the north-northeast. Across western Kansas, these storms produced winds up to 80 MPH and penny sized hail. The strongest winds were associated with an outflow boundary coming from the cluster that also produced a haboob (wall of dust) that reduced visibility down to zero. This was a unique system because the overall system and wall of dust generally moved from south to north.  A short landspout tornado occurred ahead of the wall of dust in Sherman County.
episodes.203202: In the late afternoon of the 2nd, a cluster of storms formed in far western Kansas and proceeded to the north-northeast into southwestern Nebraska. Across southwestern Nebraska, these storm produced winds up to 64 MPH. The strongest winds were associated with an outflow coming from the cluster that also produced a haboob (wall of dust) that reduced visibility down to zero. This was a unique storm system because the overall storm system and wall of dust generally moved from south to north.
episodes.203250: An upper low over the area combined with active sea breezes produced locally strong storms. One storm produced a wind gust that downed a tree across I-95.
episodes.203290: An approaching cold front and upper level disturbance, initiated thunderstorms over northern Custer County during the late afternoon hours of June 2nd. This activity then developed along a line from northern Lincoln into southeastern Holt County. This activity tracked slowly to the south into southwestern and central Nebraska and continued into the overnight hours. Heavy rain produced flash flooding in northern Custer County. Large hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts to 70 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.203706: An upper-level trough entered SW Kansas providing enough lift and moisture for thunderstorm development. As the storms progressed and strengthened, they established a cold pool and congealed into a line of storms producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.203754: Two rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across far northern and northeastern Illinois on the 3rd, the first during the early afternoon and the second during the evening. The storms produced marginally-damaging wind gusts in addition to widespread heavy rain and one brief EF0 tornado in Boone County.
episodes.204066: Severe thunderstorms and heavy rainfall affected areas from Shackelford County, south into Brown, McCulloch, Menard, and San Saba counties. Also, localized flash flooding was reported.
episodes.204127: Heavy rainfall caused flash flooding during the early morning hours June 3rd.
episodes.204222: An upper level low pulled moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Alvin into the Desert Southwest, fueling thunderstorms which produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.204224: An upper level low pulled moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Alvin into the Desert Southwest, fueling thunderstorms which produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.204366: A summertime pattern developed over the area during early June with scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms. One storm was severe with downed trees and power lines in Wakulla county.
episodes.204631: A low pressure system had moved through eastern Utah and western Colorado in the days before this event, pumping anomalously rich moisture into southern portions of the region. While showers had lingered through the night into the morning of the 3rd, the clouds did not inhibit the development of instability through the morning hours. This instability ultimately led to the development of some strong to severe thunderstorms across southwest Colorado, producing some debris flows and severe hail.
episodes.204642: Strong winds moved over southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of the 3rd ahead of a push of showers and storms later in the day. For a period of about two hours, the Harrsion-Dever crib regularly recorded gusts greater than 48 kt, peaking at 55 kt.
episodes.204826: Thunderstorms developed across south-central Kansas during the morning hours of June 3rd and slowly moved to the northeast. Additional rounds of thunderstorms developed and trained across portions of south-central and southeast Kansas. Numerous reports of flash-flooding were observed across the area with significant flooding across Sedgwick and Butler counties.
episodes.204829: During the afternoon hours of June 3rd, a line of storms brought severe winds to portions of eastern Kansas.
episodes.204939: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some locally heavy rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.
episodes.204942: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some torrential rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.||One particularly intense supercell developed near Vermillion, South Dakota and moved southeast through early evening, producing large hail, damaging wind, and heavy rainfall just over the Missouri River into northeast Nebraska before weakening.
episodes.205234: Several lines or clusters of thunderstorms with damaging winds affected southern WI during the afternoon and evening. The storms occurred along a warm front and cold front as low pressure tracked from southwest WI to northeast WI bringing storms into the waters of Lake Michigan.

Numerous reports of significant flash flooding were reported across portions of Butler County. These reports included, but not limited to, the following road closures: Kansas Highway 77 at McCollum, Highway 254 in El Dorado and Prairie Creek Road near Benton. Many other side streets and roads across Butler County were also impassible especially in El Dorado. In addition to the road closures, numerous reports of stalled vehicles due to high water were reported across many areas of the county. Homes were  evacuated on the north and southwest side of El Dorado due to rapidly rising flood waters. Flooding on area roadways and into homes impacted the Wagon Wheel neighborhood near Santa Fe Lake. A total of 240 homes and businesses were impacted in the county with damage to county roadways as well resulting in $4 million infrastructure damages.

Numerous reports of significant flash flooding were reported across portions of Sedgwick County. These reports included but not limited to the following road closures: several stretches of Kellogg in the Wichita metro area and the intersection of 13th Street and Webb. Many other side streets and roads across metro Wichita and the county were impassible. In addition to the road closures, numerous reports of stalled vehicles due to high water were reported across many areas of metro Wichita and county. Multiple homes and apartments had water enter them due to rapidly rising flood waters.

Multiple confirmations of thunderstorm wind damage along U.S. Highway 277/82 between the communities of Holiday and Wichita Falls. Damage included the metal facade of a house blown off, a travel trailer blown onto its side and numerous tree limbs, at least one power pole and a large highway road sign blown down. The location is approximate, and the event time is estimated from radar observations.
The westbound lane of Highway 54 was flooded at Jay Road.
Sheppard Air Force Base (KSPS) observation.
Storm Spotter in Burlington reports that Rock Creek is overflowing into several homes.
A wind gust on the west side of Wichita Falls Memorial Stadium. The report was relayed by amateur radio.

events.county: Wilmette Harbor To Northerly Island Il

events.narrative: Powerlines were blown down. The report was relayed through mPING. The event time is estimated from radar observations.
Large tree branch down. Time estimated by radar data.
Texas Parks and Wildlife reported 5 trees blown down and numerous large branches broken off at the Fort Griffin State Historic Site.
Roadway flooding occurred at the intersection of Lindsey Street and Elm Avenue. Multiple vehicles became stranded in floodwaters. The event time is approximate.
Three-inch diameter tree limbs were blown down. The report was relayed through mPING. The event time is estimated from radar observations.
Several roads were flooded, and at least five cars were stuck in the water.
An estimated wind gust near the intersection of U.S. Highway 281 and FM1954. The report was relayed by amateur radio.

A tornado developed near County Road 3210 about 4 miles east-southeast of Katie, and moved north-northeast. Near the beginning of the path, emergence management officials reported the east-facing garage door of a home was damaged and significant tree damage.
A hog confinement damaged.  Crop damage was noted to the northeast  corner of the county. Time estimated from radar data.

Numerous confirmations, including at least one relayed image, of power poles snapped along U.S. Highway 281 near Half House Road. The location is approximate, and the event time is estimated from radar observations.
The report was relayed through mPING.
The report was relayed through mPING.
The report was relayed through mPING.
A brief EF0 tornado with maximum winds of 85 mph touched down southwest of Ft Madison Iowa. This derailed a train. It also damaged an irrigator, a garage, and trees.
Widespread significant tree damage throughout all of  Fort Madison from 53rd street to 6th street.  Trees down on houses and trees on roads. Time estimated from radar data.
Numerous trees down at Rodeo Park. Time estimated from radar information.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a large tree onto power lines at the intersection of Hamilton and Dickerson in Palmyra. This caused a power outage that affected about 100 residences.
Heavy rain caused waters on Camp Creek to rise out of their banks. This resulted in flooding at Camp Creek Lane and Highway O where a police truck was moved by flood water.
A brief tornado was observed by storm chasers northwest of Archer City. No damage was reported and the specific location of the tornado is estimated.
A trained spotter in northeast Farmington observed quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm.
Numerous tree limbs down near Little Green Lake.
A farm shed was destroyed. Time estimated from radar data.
Recorded wind gust at the Burlington Iowa Airport.
Recorded wind gust by the Iowa DOT.

Tree and powerline damage occurred in and around the community of Pauls Valley, including a few trees/tree limbs that were blown onto houses, vehicles and at least one large business sign. A relayed image shows a large metal carport vaulted onto the roof of the Pauls Valley Police Department Building. The location is approximate, and the event time is estimated from radar observations.

This EF1 tornado with peak estimated wind speed of 100 MPH developed over New Boston  and persisted for a short time after  departing town to the northeast.  Concentrated damage in town included a roof  blown off a downtown masonry building and numerous trees uprooted or snapped.
Trained spotter measured wind gust.

This long-lived EF1 tornado began west of  the town of Joy and tracked through  Millersburg and ended about a mile and a  half west of Illinois 94.  Significant damage  to numerous trees as well as utility poles,  along with minor outbuilding damage.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in 1 foot of standing water around homes along U.S. 64 in Kirtland. Another home had water entering the garage. Up to 3 inches of water was observed running across U.S. 64 near the Coolidge Arroyo along with a large area of flood waters backs up from a nearby drainage along U.S. 64 just west of County Road 6500.
Trees down in Muscatine. Time estimated from radar data.

An EF1 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 100 mph touched down on the south side of Monmouth, and move northeast through town, damaging trees, sheds, and a garage. A roof was torn off a mobile home, and roof damaged on a house. It continued northeast where it tore the roof off a shop building and damaged trees southeast of Gerlaw.
Estimated 50 to 60 mph wind gusts with torrential rain. Relayed from HAM radio.
Thunderstorm winds heavily damaged a barn and snapped trees in an area west of Roff.
Hail size increased from quarter-size to golf ball-size between 1753 to 1756 LST. The report was relayed by amateur radio. The location is approximate.
Wind gust of 60 mph recorded on home weather station.
This brief EF0 tornado developed with a short-lived rotation area moving near due  north south of Edgington. Some sections of trees were snapped.

This tornado developed southwest of Edgington and crossed Illinois 192, doing heavy damage to three large empty grain bins and destroying an outbuilding. At the beginning of the path a well constructed farm outbuilding was destroyed. This tornado likely had winds of 105 to 110 mph at this site. Damage was done to trees all the way into Milan. This circulation was absorbed into the Coyne Center tornado.
This EF1 tornado, with maximum winds of 95 mph, tracked through Reynolds producing damage to mainly trees.
